newsitem.title: INDIA: India SEBI sets up panel on carry-forward trading.
newsitem.headline: India SEBI sets up panel on carry-forward trading.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) said on Wednesday it would set up a committee to review the carry-forward system of share trading, which currently carries strict conditions.

SEBI chairman D.R. Mehta told a news conference the stockmarket regulator's board also decided on a uniform lock-in period of three years for promoters' contributions to equity. Currently, the lock-in period varies from two to five years.
An advisory committee set up by SEBI said earlier this month the lock-in period for promoters' contributions needed to be reduced to three years from five.
Companies should also be allowed to issue equity at par value, the committee said then.
SEBI had said it would examine the panel's suggestions before taking a decision.

SEBI banned "badla" or carry forward trade in March 1994 on the grounds it was leading to excessive speculation. It introduced a modified system of carry forward trade last year with several checks and balances but many brokers are keen to revive "badla" in its original form.
Mehta said in January that the brokers' demand was a "controversial issue" that needed to be studied.
